chapters.source_heading: Chapter I: The Road of Seven Wells
chapters.notes: Second in-place expansion pass committed and verified. Current length: 4,686 words. Added a developed departure scene establishing the four men's first shared field procedure, their separate modes of attention, and the house as a place of return. Chapter II checked for transition continuity.

chapters.title: The First Return
chapters.source_heading: Chapter II: The First Return
chapters.notes: Continuity-checked at 4,549 words. The elder brother's practical, consent-centred judgment remains distinct; his younger brother preserves uncertainty and chooses a return without promising to remain; the boat keeper's safety-first values are expressed through action. The House of Returns extends preservation into a right-of-return ethic. All characters are male.

chapters.title: Big Daddy's Voice
chapters.source_heading: Chapter III: Big Daddy's Voice
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 4155 words. Preserved the competing explanations of Big Daddy's Voice and the six-day chair experiment while developing the archive's daily work, the investigators' distinct methods, the old visitor's agency, and the practical consequence of preserving contradictions. The Voice's origin remains unresolved.

chapters.title: The Men Inside the Devices
chapters.source_heading: Chapter IV: The Men Inside the Devices
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 5681 words. Differentiated the men through their habits and choices across the devices; added practical route-testing, individual preferences, shared work, a power interruption, and the archive's transformation into a meeting environment.

chapters.title: The House of Open Screens
chapters.source_heading: Chapter V: The House of Open Screens
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 4013 words. Developed the first house through shared meals, repairs, room use, winter isolation, walking routes, and the six men's habits of care. Architecture changes through lived use rather than spectacle; departure remains possible and the house becomes a place of return.

chapters.title: The Blue Hall
chapters.source_heading: Chapter VI: The Blue Hall
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 4108 words. Developed the Blue Hall as a traversable memory architecture, preserving the fifty-seventh, seventy-second, eightieth, ninety-first, and hundredth openings and their seven distinct relations. The men's different methods of exploration remain visible; the Voice's answer remains open rather than being resolved into a source.

chapters.title: The Seventh Man — The Road Remembered
chapters.source_heading: Chapter VII: The Seventh Man — The Road Remembered
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 4,956 words. Corrected the reservoir reference to the elder brother and his brother, preserving Chapter II's all-male continuity. Developed the Seventh Man's recurring appearances through the amber road, reservoir, failed-valve record, Blue Hall, and first residence. The investigators retain distinct methods and disagreements; sightings remain provisional, and the man's identity and motives are unresolved.

chapters.title: The Room Beyond the File
chapters.source_heading: Chapter VIII: The Room Beyond the File
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 4,794 words. Developed the room beyond the file as a lived residence with a workshop, library, quiet room, table, active repairs, and an unfinished passage. Preserved the four men's journey on the screen, the observer's freedom to leave, and the distinction between a source file and the place it opens. All cast members are male; the Seventh Man's identity remains unresolved.

chapters.title: The Country Between
chapters.source_heading: Chapter IX: The Country Between
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 4,794 words. Recast the waystation keeper as an older man and developed the four men's journey through the unfinished country: the stream, route map, broken bridge, waystation, abandoned foundations, and forest marker. Luke's directness, Tyler's method, Kirk's observation, and Joseph's reflective judgment remain distinct. The distant voice and the unfinished routes remain unresolved.

chapters.title: The House That Remembered
chapters.source_heading: Chapter X: The House That Remembered
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 4,018 words. Developed the remembered house through its male architects, changing measurements, resident needs, preserved plans, restricted rooms, copper vessel, and rising Serum. Measurement remains useful without exhausting the building's history; the Serum's cause and the man's full identity remain open.

chapters.title: The Commit History
chapters.source_heading: Chapter XI: The Commit History
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 4,267 words. The commit-history principle is developed through practical changes to rooms, roads, maps, photographs, access permissions, branches, and merges. Preserving an earlier record is distinguished from keeping an old arrangement publicly active or binding. The characters' different priorities remain visible, and the chapter ends with continuity as accountable change.

chapters.title: The Serum House
chapters.source_heading: Chapter XII: The Serum House
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 3,399 words. Developed the Serum House as an inhabited convergence of the reservoir, laboratory, city, devices, and the men's shared life. Preserved the old physician's source record, the brothers' separate choices, the house's practical maintenance, and the open threshold to the road. Reconciled the inherited sister reference into the elder and younger brothers. The chapter remains deliberately concise rather than padded to a numeric target.

chapters.title: The War for the House
chapters.source_heading: Chapter XIII: The War for the House
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 3,341 words. Developed the three southern armies' attempts to claim the house, the residents' nonviolent defense through changing space, the captain's return to recover his men, the river crossing dispute, and the coastal delegation's access challenge. Luke, Tyler, Kirk, Joseph, Bill, and the largest man respond according to distinct priorities. The house's right to remain open without becoming possessable is established; the kings' next move is to bring maps.

chapters.title: The Cartographers
chapters.source_heading: Chapter XIV: The Cartographers
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 3,109 words. Developed Orlan's disciplined survey, Pell's alternate map of use, the assessor's jurisdictional demands, and the Blue Hall measurement problem. Preserved separate maps and source provenance; the royal copies distort the original survey and set up the lake fleet's attack. Concise by design, with the unresolved geometry carried into Chapter XV.

chapters.title: The Lake Battle
chapters.source_heading: Chapter XV: The Lake Battle
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 3,367 words. Developed the fleet's attack through changing water, streets, towers, and routes; preserved the residents' nonviolent response and the soldiers' agency to leave. Orlan's original and altered maps remain distinct. The battle ends without a conventional victor and changes the lake's geography for the next chapters.

chapters.title: The Seventh Vessel
chapters.source_heading: Chapter XVI: The Seventh Vessel
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 2,884 words. Developed the young man's discovery of the seventh vessel, his father's caution, the archivists' restraint, the soldiers' access concerns, and the Seventh Man's account of continuity. The vessel remains in place; its origin and operation remain unresolved. The all-male cast is maintained.

chapters.title: The Men Make a Kingdom
chapters.source_heading: Chapter XVII: The Men Make a Kingdom
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 2,716 words. Developed the men's common kingdom through route governance, room privacy, voluntary records, distributed responsibility, and the elder brother's conversation with the largest man. The city has laws without a single ruler; membership does not require ownership or permanent residence. All characters are male.

chapters.title: The Door in the Wrong Century
chapters.source_heading: Chapter XVIII: The Door in the Wrong Century
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 2,820 words. Developed the door into a future city, the cartographers' cautious survey, the soldiers' return route, the old physician's reflection, and the brothers' decision to return for now. The future remains a separate place connected by an open threshold. All characters are male.

chapters.title: The Adventures of the Men
chapters.source_heading: Chapter XIX: The Adventures of the Men
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 2,079 words. Developed the seven men's departure as a chosen expedition, with distinct travel habits, practical preparation, route recording, and the discovery of the red door. The house remains available as a place of return; the city of men is entered without a claim of ownership. All characters are male.

chapters.title: The City of Men
chapters.source_heading: Chapter XX: The City of Men
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified. Developed the city as a working civic environment across the Archive, Market, Garden, Muscle Quarter, and unnamed hall; preserved the seven travelers' distinct methods and the registrar's uncertainty. Replaced the stray sister reference with the elder brother from the northern house. The Serum reaches the next room without resolving its nature. All cast members are male.

chapters.title: The Serum
chapters.source_heading: Chapter XXI: The Serum
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified. The first Serum encounter becomes a conflict of interpretations rather than a simple power-up. The seven men disagree over cure, strength, control, risk, and memory; the largest man changes while retaining his earlier state. Added provisional rules for observation, consent, shared access, and archival provenance. The vessel remains unexplained; the ending now leads directly into the liminal chest transformation.

chapters.title: The Liminal Chest
chapters.source_heading: Chapter XXII: The Liminal Chest
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified. The transformation is developed through its physical and spatial consequences, the repairer's structural eye, the strength-seeker's uncertainty, the Seventh Man's interpretation, and the others' practical care. Earlier and current body states remain simultaneous. Pause and withdrawal remain available without treating change itself as danger.

chapters.title: The Field of Attention
chapters.source_heading: Chapter XXIII: The Field of Attention
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 1,836 words. Develops the city as a field of attention without making recognition into ownership. Joseph and the Teller retain a distinct marital history; Tyler's growth, Luke's chosen distance, Kirk's building, Bill's practical generosity, the largest man's restraint, and the Seventh Man's observation remain separate trajectories. Deliberately concise chapter leading into the House of the Seventh Light.

chapters.title: The House of the Seventh Light
chapters.source_heading: Chapter XXIV: The House of the Seventh Light
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified at 1,947 words. The House of the Seventh Light becomes a lived place: the first keeper's practical hospitality, the seven chairs and unclaimed seat, ordinary meals and rooms, and the rule that a prepared place does not create an obligation to stay. The keeper's map is introduced as the next step. All figures are male.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Map
chapters.source_heading: Chapter XXV: The Keeper's Map
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified against Chapters XXIV and XXVI. Developed the cloth map as a record of carried decisions rather than fixed geography; each man's method of reading it remains distinct. The seven artifacts change relation without losing their histories. The new line beneath the city leads toward an unremembered artifact, preparing the descent in Chapter XXVI. All cast members are male.

chapters.title: The Battle Beneath the City
chapters.source_heading: Chapter XXVI: The Battle Beneath the City
chapters.notes: Expanded and verified against Chapters XXV and XXVII. The attack becomes a conflict of incompatible memories; each man's response remains distinct, and the city is protected through evacuation, measurement, structural support, and careful recording. The black artifact is not destroyed or claimed; it becomes a road. All cast members are male.

chapters.title: The Road Made of Men
chapters.source_heading: Chapter XXVII: The Road Made of Men
chapters.notes: Next canonical chapter. Develop the road as a record of male lives and possible histories. Replace the existing references to a sister, a woman carrying a lantern, and a child with adult male figures; preserve the rule that not every appearance requires an answer.
